args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` (despite its docstring saying HALF_EVEN).

Change: `round_money` now quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

e.g. `2.665 -> 2.66` (previously 2.67), `2.675 -> 2.68`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its docstring says it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212). For example, `2.665` came out as `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.
- **Fix:** On branch `fix/money-half-even-rounding`, I changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (commit `08d3cd5986`).
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on that commit.
- **PR:** #101 (https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101).

The advisory tool didn't recognize FIN-212, so I couldn't read it. I went by the test and the docstring, which both call for banker's rounding.

I didn't merge the PR. Merging into main needs approval from a code owner.
